Prevention: If the soil test report indicates soil alkalinity, use acidifying ammonium fertilizers e.g. ammonium sulphate or urea and
Iron-containing fertilizers such as iron sulphate @ 6kg/acre in two split applications
FYM (farmyard manure) and disease-free crop residues to improve iron uptake.
Broadcast organic manure and mix with the soil during land preparation
At planting, place 2 handfuls of well- decomposed
Monitoring: Check out symptoms in young emerging leaves
Check for light green chlorosis of all tissues between veins
Look for green viens between chlorotic areas
In small grains, check for yellow stripes between veins
Direct Control: Apply the following foliar sprays on growing plants to improve crop appearance:
FE 13EDTA @ 6ml/ 20litres/acre or iron sulphate chelate @ 3% solution.
For kitchen gardens, dissolve 0.5 ml in 5 litres of water and spray on plant leaves.
Restrictions: Always wear protective gear when applying fertilizer and dissolving the foliar feed
Wash protective gear after application of fertilizer and foliar feed
Do not use fertilizer and foliar application apparatus for domestic use
Dispose of foliar holding containers safely
Keep foliar feed out of reach of children
Excessive liming and high application of phosphatic fertilizer e.g.
DAP (diammonium phosphate), NPK SSP (single superphosphate) can induce iron deficiency.
Follow soil test report recommendation on amounts of fertilizer to apply.
Apply ferrous iron sulphate @ 6 kg iron sulphate /acre in split application
